section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the world's sustenance through the Ten Commandments after the Giving of the Torah draws Atzmus, unlike the work of the Patriarchs or Adam before the sin, which only drew from the root of creation.
section.t: And the explanation of the matter
(of "He increases peace in the world")
in greater depth,
will be understood from what is said in the maamar60
that the sustenance of the world is by drawing down into the Ten Utterances
(through which the world was created)
the Ten Commandments,
and it can be said that his intention in emphasizing specifically the Ten Commandments
(which were given at the Giving of the Torah)
is,
that the sustenance of the world is specifically through the service of Torah and mitzvos after the Giving of the Torah.
For although even through the service of the Patriarchs
(the Patriarchs themselves are the Chariot61)
additional light was drawn into the world
(beyond the light of the Ten Utterances)62,
nevertheless,
since the service of the Patriarchs was with their own power
(for they were not commanded regarding this),
therefore,
the light drawn by their service is
(generally)
only from the aspect of the root of created beings
(as is known the proof of this63
from the spring of Ein Eitam64),
and this is not at all comparable to the drawing down through the fulfillment of the mitzvos after the Giving of the Torah65.
And moreover,
even the service of Adam HaRishon,
as it was in the Garden of Eden
("And He placed him in the Garden of Eden to work it and to guard it"66)
and before the sin,
which is more elevated than the service of the Patriarchs67,
and the light drawn by his service is an incomparable addition relative to the world as it is in itself
[to the extent that it can be said that this is analogous to the drawing down through the mitzvos after the Giving of the Torah,
and as our sages, of blessed memory, said68
"to work it" — these are the 248 positive commandments, "and to guard it" — these are the 365 negative commandments,
that the service of Adam HaRishon in the Garden of Eden
("to work it and to guard it")
is analogous to the 248 positive commandments and 365 negative commandments after the Giving of the Torah],
nevertheless,
even the drawing down through the service of Adam HaRishon in the Garden of Eden was only an illumination69,
because until the Giving of the Torah there was the decree70
that the upper ones shall not descend below and the lower ones shall not ascend above.
But not so the drawing down through the Torah and mitzvos after the Giving of the Torah
(when the decree70 was nullified)
is the drawing down of Atzmus.
And based on this, the matter of "He increases peace in the world" will be understood in greater depth,
that the increase of peace in the world is not only that the revelation of Ein Sof, which is above the root of the worlds, is drawn into it,
but moreover,
that Atzmus is drawn into it,
the perfection of the matter of a dwelling place in the lower realms,
a dwelling place for His very Self71.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that because G-d does not withhold reward, the increase of peace brought about by Torah scholars is also drawn to them, revealing the pleasure of the Creator which is beyond the reward of the World to Come.
section.t: And now, since the Holy One, blessed be He, does not withhold the reward of any creature72,
therefore,
the increase of peace that is made in the world through the Torah scholars is also drawn to the Torah scholars themselves73.
That is,
the gratification to the Creator from the fact that a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He, is made in the lower realms,
will be revealed to the Torah scholars who made the dwelling place,
and this revelation is beyond the reward of the World to Come as it is in itself.
For the reward of the World to Come in itself is an aspect of the gratification of the created being, which is incomparable to the gratification of the Creator,
therefore, one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world is better than all the life of the World to Come74,
because the World to Come
(the reward of a mitzvah)
is the gratification of the created being, which is incomparable to the gratification of the Creator — repentance and good deeds in this world75.
But since the Holy One, blessed be He, does not withhold the reward of any creature,
there will be drawn to the righteous
(who made the gratification of the Creator)
also the aspect of the gratification of the Creator76.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that to receive the Creator's own pleasure, which is beyond all measure, one must be in a state of utter self-nullification, like a servant whose entire existence is that of the master.
section.t: However, in order that they be able to receive this aspect of gratification, which is not at all commensurate with them
[for this gratification is the essential pleasure of His very Self,
to which no boundary whatsoever applies],
for this they must be in a state of utter self-nullification,
that they are not an independent entity at all
[in the manner of our sages, of blessed memory: "Who is the face of the Lord, G-d?"77
— that is Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai78,
"And the L-rd is in His holy Heichal"79
— that is Rabbi Yitzchak bar Elazar in the assembly of the study hall of Caesarea80],
for through this they are able to receive the gratification and pleasure of the Creator,
for the pleasure of the Creator is their pleasure.
And analogous to a servant,
who, since he is not an independent entity and his entire existence is the existence of the master81,
the pleasure of the master is the pleasure of the servant82.
